name: ESP32-C5

strapping.2: Listed as a strapping pin by the ESP-IDF GPIO summary and by datasheet v1.5 Sec. 2.3.5 (Priority-3 list). However datasheet Section 3 (Boot Configurations) assigns no strapping function to GPIO2 (MTMS). Exact function UNCONFIRMED - treat as strapping.
strapping.3: MTDI: SDIO sampling/driving clock-edge strapping together with GPIO25 (datasheet v1.5 Table 3-4). Default floating. Listed as strapping in the datasheet Priority-3 list but NOT in the ESP-IDF GPIO summary (IDF lists GPIO2 instead) - documentation discrepancy, kept for safety.
strapping.7: JTAG signal source select, used with EFUSE_DIS_PAD_JTAG / EFUSE_DIS_USB_JTAG / EFUSE_JTAG_SEL_ENABLE (only consulted when JTAG_SEL_ENABLE is burned: low = JTAG on GPIO2-GPIO5, high = USB_SERIAL_JTAG). Default floating; datasheet: 'This pin does not have any internal pull resistors and the strapping value must be controlled by the external circuit that cannot be in a high impedance state.'
strapping.25: SDIO sampling/driving clock-edge strapping together with MTDI (GPIO3). Default floating.
strapping.26: Chip boot mode strapping (with GPIO27, GPIO28): GPIO26=0, GPIO27=0, GPIO28=0 selects Joint Download Boot 1 (UART / SDIO download). Default floating. Listed in datasheet v1.5 but NOT in the ESP-IDF GPIO summary - kept for safety.
strapping.27: Chip boot mode strapping (with GPIO26, GPIO28) and UART0 ROM message printing control (with EFUSE_UART_PRINT_CONTROL). Default: pull-up (1). GPIO27=1 with GPIO28=0 selects Joint Download Boot 0 (USB-Serial-JTAG / UART download).
strapping.28: Chip boot mode strapping: 1 = SPI Boot (default, pull-up); 0 = download boot (Joint Download Boot 0 if GPIO27=1, Joint Download Boot 1 if GPIO26=GPIO27=0).

psram.condition: Chips with in-package PSRAM (ESP32-C5HR2, ESP32-C5HR8, ESP32-C5NF8R2LA per datasheet v1.5 Table 1-1) or with off-package PSRAM: SPICS1 = GPIO15 is PSRAM chip-select; SPICLK (GPIO21), SPID (GPIO22), SPIQ (GPIO17), SPIWP (GPIO18), SPIHD (GPIO20) are shared with flash. All are already in flash_spi.

usb_jtag.note: GPIO13 = D-, GPIO14 = D+ (ESP-IDF USB-Serial-JTAG console page). Used by USB-JTAG by default; reconfiguring them as normal GPIOs disables USB-JTAG. When USB is disabled their internal weak pull-up/down are disabled by default but configurable.

notes: STRAPPING DISCREPANCY: ESP-IDF stable GPIO summary lists strapping pins GPIO2, GPIO7, GPIO25, GPIO27, GPIO28. Datasheet v1.5 Section 3 lists GPIO26/27/28 (boot mode), GPIO25 + MTDI=GPIO3 (SDIO edge), GPIO27 (ROM print), GPIO7 (JTAG source); its Sec. 2.3.5 Priority-3 list says 'GPIO2, GPIO3, GPIO7, GPIO25, GPIO26, GPIO27, GPIO28 : Strapping pins.' The union is used here. Verify against a newer datasheet / TRM Chip Boot Control before relaxing.

FLASH PIN DISCREPANCY: ESP-IDF says 'GPIO16 ~ GPIO22 are usually used for SPI flash and PSRAM'. TRM v1.1 Sec. IO MUX says '8 dedicated GPIO pins (GPIO15~GPIO22) for external flash and PSRAM. These pins can not be used for other purpose'. Datasheet IO MUX table: GPIO15=SPICS1 (PSRAM CS), GPIO16=SPICS0, GPIO17=SPIQ, GPIO18=SPIWP, GPIO19=VDD_SPI (chip pin 29), GPIO20=SPIHD, GPIO21=SPICLK, GPIO22=SPID. flash_spi therefore uses the TRM range GPIO15-GPIO22.

Datasheet v1.5 Sec. 2.3.5 states 'GPIO27 : The VDD_SPI pin', but its own pin overview / IO MUX table place VDD_SPI on chip pin 29 = GPIO19 (GPIO27 is a normal VDDPST3 pin). This looks like a datasheet copy error; VDD_SPI is treated as GPIO19 here.
Datasheet footnote: for ESP32-C5HF4 the SPICS0, SPIQ, SPIWP, VDD_SPI, SPIHD, SPICLK, SPID pins are not connected (NC) on the package; for ESP32-C5NF8R2LA SPICS1 is also NC.

input_only / no_internal_pull are empty: the ESP-IDF GPIO summary lists no input-only or pull-less pins for this chip (the 'input-only GPIOs 34-39' remarks on the page are for the original ESP32); datasheet IO MUX types are I/O/T for all GPIOs; TRM v1.1 Register 8.25 IO_MUX_GPIOn_REG (n: 0-14, 23-28) has FUN_WPU/FUN_WPD (GPIO15-22 are dedicated flash/PSRAM pins not described). The datasheet statement that GPIO7 'does not have any internal pull resistors' refers to its strapping state at reset; firmware-controllable pulls exist per the TRM register.
jtag order is [MTMS, MTDI, MTCK, MTDO] = [GPIO2, GPIO3, GPIO4, GPIO5]. JTAG defaults to USB_SERIAL_JTAG; burning DIS_USB_JTAG moves it to GPIO2-GPIO5.

No ADC2: ESP32-C5 has one 12-bit SAR ADC (TRM/datasheet: 'One 12-bit successive approximation ADC'); ADC1 channels CH0-CH5 on GPIO1-GPIO6. ESP-IDF stable ADC oneshot hardware limitations for C5 contain only the RNG and oneshot/continuous exclusivity notes; no Wi-Fi restriction.
LP GPIOs: GPIO0-GPIO6 (LP_GPIO0-6), usable in deep sleep / by LP core.
Radio: datasheet '2.4 and 5 GHz dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax), Bluetooth 5 (LE), Zigbee, and Thread (802.15.4)' - no Bluetooth Classic.
Data sourced from ESP-IDF stable = v6.1 docs, ESP32-C5 datasheet v1.5, ESP32-C5 TRM v1.1, retrieved 2026-10-28.
